title: Luca AI product documentation
text: Luca is an AI analyst for e-commerce brands. It reads the data you connect from your store, ad platforms, analytics, payment and accounting tools, and answers your questions about the business in plain English. Luca works done-with-you. Luca's team onboards each client directly, and a human stays in the loop: Luca does not change your connected systems on its own. This documentation is for buyers evaluating Luca, and for anyone who needs an exact account of what the product does today.

title: Products
text: This section describes the parts of Luca and how they fit together. It is for buyers evaluating Luca and for operators who want to know what each part does and where its limits are. Luca is an AI analyst agent for e-commerce brands. You connect your sources, ask questions in plain English in the chat, and see a reconciled view of your business in Numbers.

title: Luca, the AI analyst agent
text: This page describes Luca, the AI analyst agent you use through a chat interface over your connected data. It covers how you ask questions, the kinds of answers you get, and where the agent's limits are. It is for operators and buyers evaluating how Luca would fit day-to-day analysis. The agent sits on top of Numbers, the reconciled view of your data, and can draw on context you add to the knowledge base. Luca suggests and you decide: it does not change your connected systems.

title: Numbers: the reconciled control centre
text: Numbers is the reconciled control centre in Luca. It brings data from your sources together into one clean database and shows it as a unified view above the chat. This page is for operators and finance or growth leads who want to understand what Numbers shows and how it is set up. Numbers is the data layer: the dashboard is the reconciled data itself, with no AI in it. Luca, the agent, sits on top of it and answers questions using that data.

title: Knowledge base and business context
text: The knowledge base is where you give Luca context about your business. You can upload company documents and manage them in the product. This page is for operators who want Luca's answers to reflect their goals and rules, not only their raw data. The knowledge base works alongside your connected sources and Numbers. Separately, Luca has its own internal knowledge base, written by its team, that describes what it can and cannot do.

title: Capital, and how it relates to Luca
text: This page explains how capital relates to Luca. Capital is optional, and you do not need it to use Luca. It is for buyers and finance leads who want a clear picture before evaluating the product. Luca is an agentic AI company for e-commerce, not a financing company, and Luca is not a lender or a bank. Capital is an optional output of Luca's intelligence, provided through lending partners, and availability and terms are confirmed directly with Luca's team.

title: Feature directory
text: The feature directory groups Luca's supporting capabilities by area. It is for buyers checking specific requirements, such as how sources connect, what Luca can and cannot change, and how seats work. Each feature page sits alongside the product pages: the Luca agent, Numbers, the knowledge base and capital.

title: Data connection and setup
text: This page explains how you connect a data source to Luca. It is for anyone setting up an account or evaluating how much effort setup takes. Connected sources are what the Luca agent reasons across and what Numbers reconciles. Some reconciliation work is done by Luca's team after you connect, as described on the Numbers page.

title: Control and safety: Luca reads, you decide
text: This page explains what Luca can and cannot do in your connected systems. It is for operators, finance leads and anyone responsible for the systems Luca connects to. Luca reads, you decide. The agent analyses your data and suggests next steps; you validate them and make any changes yourself.

title: Teams, seats and regions
text: This page covers how Luca plans are structured by seat, the unlimited-seat option, and the regions Luca serves. It is for buyers planning who in their team will use Luca. Plans are sold by seat, so the plan you choose sets how many people can use Luca. Prices are not stated here; see the pricing page for current plans.

title: Integrations
text: This section describes the data sources you can connect to Luca and what each one contributes. It is for teams evaluating Luca and for anyone setting up a new workspace. Luca reads across the sources you connect so you can ask questions in plain English and see a reconciled view of your business in Numbers. Each page notes where a connection is set up by Luca's team rather than by you.

title: Commerce platforms
text: This page covers the commerce platforms you can connect to Luca. It is for brands that sell through their own store, through a marketplace, or both. Luca's website recommends a commerce platform as your first source. You can then add advertising, analytics and finance sources around it.

title: Shopify
text: This page explains how Shopify connects to Luca and what that connection supports. It is for brands that run their store on Shopify. Shopify is one of the two sources Luca's website suggests connecting first. Other sources, such as advertising, analytics and finance, are added around it.

title: Amazon
text: This page explains the Amazon connection in Luca. It is for brands that sell on Amazon, on its own or alongside a Shopify store. Luca's website names Amazon, with Shopify, as a starting source. Advertising, analytics and finance sources are added after it.

title: Advertising
text: This page covers the advertising platforms you can connect to Luca. It is for teams that want to look at ad activity alongside sales and finance data. Luca's website suggests adding advertising sources after your commerce platform. Once connected, they sit alongside your other sources in the Connect & Setup screen.

title: Meta Ads
text: This page explains the Meta Ads connection in Luca. It is for brands that advertise on Meta / Facebook. Meta Ads is one of the advertising sources you can add after your commerce platform. It appears with your other sources in the Connect & Setup screen.

title: Google Ads
text: This page explains the Google Ads connection in Luca and the access it uses. It is for brands that advertise on Google. Google Ads is one of the advertising sources you can add after your commerce platform. Like Luca's other Google connections, it is covered by the read-only terms in Luca's privacy policy.

title: Web analytics and search
text: This page covers the web analytics and search sources you can connect to Luca. It is for teams that want site and search data available next to sales, advertising and finance data. Luca's website suggests adding analytics sources after your commerce platform. Both sources in this category are Google products, so Luca's privacy policy terms for Google data apply.

title: Google Analytics 4
text: This page explains the Google Analytics connection in Luca and how its data is handled. It is for brands that use Google Analytics 4 on their site. Google Analytics is one of the sources Luca reasons across when you ask questions. It sits alongside commerce, advertising and finance sources.

title: Google Search Console
text: This page explains the Google Search Console connection in Luca and the access it uses. It is for brands that want search data available to Luca. Search Console is one of the analytics and search sources you can add after your commerce platform. Its access is read-only.

title: Payments and accounting
text: This page covers the payments and accounting sources you can connect to Luca. It is for finance leads and founders who want sales data checked against payments and the books. Luca's website suggests adding finance sources after your commerce platform. Accounting data has been reconciled with Shopify and subscription data in Numbers for a live client.

title: Stripe
text: This page explains the Stripe connection in Luca. It is for brands that take payments through Stripe. Stripe is one of the finance sources you can add after your commerce platform. It appears with your other sources in the Connect & Setup screen.

title: Xero
text: This page explains the Xero connection in Luca and how accounting data has been used in Numbers. It is for brands that keep their books in Xero. Xero is one of the finance sources you can add after your commerce platform. Accounting data can be reconciled with commerce and subscription data in Numbers.

title: QuickBooks
text: This page explains the QuickBooks connection in Luca and what you should confirm before relying on it. It is for brands that keep their books in QuickBooks. QuickBooks sits in the payments and accounting category alongside Xero and Stripe.

title: Recharge (subscriptions)
text: This page explains how Recharge subscription data is brought into Luca. It is for subscription brands that use Recharge alongside Shopify and an accounting platform. Recharge data is connected by Luca's team as part of a Numbers build. It is then reconciled with your commerce and accounting data.

title: Subscriptions
text: This page covers subscription data in Luca. It is for brands that sell subscriptions and need that data to line up with store and accounting records. Subscription data is brought in by Luca's team as part of a Numbers build, rather than through a self-serve connector.

title: Workspace and documents
text: This page covers the ways you can work with Luca from your workspace and give it extra context. It is for teams that want to ask Luca questions where they already work, or add documents Luca can use. These options sit alongside your data connections. They change where you ask questions and what context Luca has, not which data sources are connected.

title: Slack
text: This page explains how to use Luca from Slack. It is for teams that want to ask Luca questions without leaving Slack. Slack is a way to talk to Luca, not a data source. Luca answers from the sources you have connected.

title: Documents and files
text: This page explains how to add company documents to Luca as context. It is for teams whose questions depend on information held in files rather than in connected systems. Documents add context alongside your data connections. They do not replace a connector for a live system.

title: Custom connectors and ERPs
text: This page explains how Luca connects to systems that do not have a standard connector, such as a custom ERP. It is for brands whose data sits in internal or less common systems. Custom connections are built by Luca's team and then sit alongside your standard connections. They are not a self-serve button.

title: Solutions by buyer
text: This section describes Luca from the point of view of specific buyers: founders and CEOs, subscription brands, finance leads, growth teams, Shopify and Amazon sellers, European and UK brands, and Mastercard Business Bonus merchants. Each page takes the needs that buyer tends to raise and answers them with what Luca does today. The capabilities themselves are documented under Products and Integrations. Solution pages connect those capabilities to the questions a particular buyer asks during evaluation.

title: For founders and CEOs of Shopify brands
text: This page is for founders and CEOs of Shopify brands who want to understand the business without building dashboards or hiring an analyst first. It covers how you use Luca, what it can see, how your data is treated and who helps you get started. Most of what is described here runs on Numbers, Luca's reconciled view of the business, and on the plain English questions you ask over your connected data.

title: For subscription DTC brands
text: This page is for subscription DTC brands that need their subscription platform, Shopify and accounting data to agree. It covers reconciled reporting, subscriber status, skip analysis, cohort visibility and connecting a subscription platform. These needs are met through Numbers, the reconciled view of the business, with the subscription connection set up by Luca's team.

title: For CFOs and finance leads
text: This page is for CFOs, finance leads and fractional CFOs evaluating whether Luca's numbers can be trusted and controlled. It covers approval and control, the role of your accounting system, data retention, reconciliation to the accounting system and accounting connections. Luca reads your accounting data alongside commerce data. It does not replace your ledger and it does not move money or change systems.

title: For growth and marketing teams
text: This page is for heads of growth and performance marketing teams. It covers using Luca from Slack and connecting Google Analytics and Search Console alongside your ad platforms. Both needs rest on the same idea: your team asks Luca questions over connected data, in the place it already works.

title: For Shopify and Amazon sellers
text: This page is for brands that sell on both Shopify and Amazon and want one picture of the business. It covers connecting both channels and how they are brought together in reporting. Shopify and Amazon both connect to Luca as commerce sources, alongside your other data.

title: For European and UK brands
text: This page is for brands based in Europe and the UK. It covers local-currency pricing, the Mastercard Business Bonus programme and European accounting and banking connections. The product is the same for European brands. What differs is how pricing is published and which local data sources are confirmed.

title: For Mastercard Business Bonus merchants
text: This page is for merchants who reach Luca through Mastercard Business Bonus. It covers the partner pricing page, eligibility, the discount, the Mastercard listing and what the partner plans include. Partner pricing gives you the same Luca plans as standard pricing, with a discount set out on Luca's dedicated Mastercard Business Bonus pricing page.

title: Pricing model
text: This page explains how Luca's pricing is structured: what you pay for, what does not change your price and how billing works. It is for founders and finance leads comparing Luca with other analytics tools or with hiring an analyst. It describes the pricing model only. For current plans and figures, see ask-luca.com/pricing, and for what happens when you sign up, see Trial and signup.

title: Trial and signup
text: This page describes what happens when you sign up for Luca, so you can prepare before you start. It is for the person who will create the account and connect the first data source. Trial availability and terms are not covered here. Check ask-luca.com/pricing for the current offer, and see Onboarding for what Luca's team does with you after signup.

title: Security and data handling
text: This section explains where Luca stores your data, who processes it, what access Luca requests and what happens to your data when you leave. It is for founders, finance leads and anyone completing a vendor security review. Luca connects to your commerce, advertising, analytics, payments and accounting systems, so this is the place to check what happens to that data once it is connected.

title: How Luca stores and processes your data
text: This page explains where Luca hosts your data, how each customer's data is kept separate, which sub-processors handle it and whether it is used to train AI models. It is for anyone assessing Luca as a vendor. It summarises Luca's privacy policy and website. For access scopes and deletion, see Access and deletion.

title: Access, scopes and deletion
text: This page explains the level of access Luca requests when you connect a platform, and what happens to your data after you disconnect or close your account. It is for the person approving connections and for anyone reviewing data retention. For hosting, data separation and sub-processors, see Data handling.

title: Onboarding, services and support
text: This section explains how Luca's team helps you get set up and where you can learn from other users. It is for teams planning a rollout and for anyone who wants to know what working with Luca looks like after signup. Onboarding with Luca is done with you: Luca's team does much of the setup work, including data mapping and reconciling your systems into Numbers.

title: Onboarding: done with you
text: This page explains how onboarding works with Luca and what Luca's team does for you during setup. It is for founders and operators planning when to start. Onboarding is where your connected systems are mapped and reconciled into Numbers, Luca's reconciled view of your figures.

title: Community and podcast
text: This page describes the Luca community and the E-Commerce Leaders Series podcast. It is for clients and prospects who want to learn from other operators. Both sit alongside the onboarding Luca's team runs with you.

title: About Luca
text: This page introduces the company behind Luca: its founder, its named team, the AI model provider it uses and a recent example of product progress. It is for buyers assessing Luca as a vendor. Luca is an AI analyst agent for e-commerce brands. For how your data is handled, see the Security section.

title: Customers and proof
text: This page lists the brands shown as customers on ask-luca.com and points you to the testimonials published there. It is for buyers who want to see which brands use Luca. Testimonials are not reproduced in this documentation. Read them on ask-luca.com.

title: Documentation coverage and open questions
text: This version documents 101 capabilities: 85 confirmed as available and 16 confirmed in a limited form, each with its scope stated. They come from a 612-parameter evaluation of what e-commerce buyers and AI engines look for in an AI analyst agent. Everything MaximusLabs could not confirm is left out of this version on purpose. It is listed in a worksheet for Luca's team, together with the places where Luca's website currently describes the same thing in different ways.

text: Answers from Luca returned in Slack when you send it a direct message or mention it in a channel. Available

title: U27 · Upload documents and files as context

title: U22 · Custom ERP and internal-system connections
text: API connections that Luca's team builds on request for systems without a standard connector, such as a custom ERP. Available · limited scope

title: U28 · Custom connectors built by Luca's team, no integration fee
text: Custom connectors that Luca's team builds and delivers, which Luca's website states carry no integration fee. Available · limited scope

title: U31 · Connect a source in two clicks (OAuth)

title: U84 · Ask questions in plain English across connected sources

title: U85 · Answers that combine marketing, finance and commerce data
text: Cross-source reasoning means one answer draws on several kinds of business data at once, such as marketing, finance and commerce, instead of reporting from one tool at a time. Available · limited scope

title: U86 · Charts generated from a question

title: U87 · Follow-up questions in the same conversation
text: Multi-turn follow-ups let you continue a conversation, asking a further question that builds on the previous answer. Available

title: U92 · Unlimited questions, no AI credits
text: Unlimited usage means the number of questions you can ask is not capped by a credit or question allowance. Available

title: U93 · Web app
text: A web app runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install. Available

title: U119 · Recommended next steps
text: Prescriptive next steps are recommendations about what to do, given alongside the analysis that supports them. Available

title: U103 · Marketing content drafting
text: Content drafting produces first versions of marketing material, such as posts or newsletters, for a person to review and edit. Available · limited scope

title: U127 · Done-with-you analysis and strategy
text: A done-with-you model means the product does the analysis and proposes a strategy, while your team validates it and carries it out. Available

title: M1 · Tells you plainly when a request is outside what it does
text: Clear refusal means an assistant says directly when a request is outside what it can do, rather than attempting it or giving a vague reply. Available

title: U32 · One reconciled database across your sources
text: A reconciled database combines data from several systems and resolves differences between them, so each figure has one agreed value. Available

title: U189 · Unified control-centre view
text: A control-centre view is a single screen that shows the main figures you need to run a business. Available

title: U50 · Net revenue
text: Net revenue is revenue after deductions such as discounts, refunds and returns. Available

title: U67 · Cohort analysis
text: Cohort analysis groups customers by when they started, such as their first order or subscription month, and tracks how each group behaves over time. Available

title: U69 · Active vs lapsed customers
text: Active and lapsed customer status separates customers who are still buying or subscribed from those who have stopped. Available · limited scope

title: U180 · Subscription skips, pauses and gaps
text: Subscription skip and pause data records when subscribers skip or pause deliveries, which affects revenue even when they have not cancelled. Available · limited scope

title: U34 · Reconciled with accounting data
text: Accounting reconciliation checks commerce figures against the accounting records, so the figures you analyse agree with your books. Available · limited scope

title: M2 · Data connections shown on Numbers
text: Connection status shows which data sources feed a dashboard. Available

title: U146 · Upload company documents to a knowledge base
text: A knowledge base is a set of company documents that an AI system can refer to when answering questions. Available

title: U147 · Goals, constraints and cost rules as context
text: Business context is the information about goals, limits and rules that shapes what a good decision looks like for a particular business. Available · limited scope

title: M3 · Built-in knowledge of its own capabilities
text: Self-knowledge in an AI agent is a defined description of what it can and cannot do, which it uses to answer requests accurately. Available

title: U178 · Capital is optional
text: Optional capital means funding is an extra that a business may choose to explore, not something the product depends on. Available

title: U179 · Luca is not a lender
text: A lender is the party that provides credit and is responsible for it. Luca is not a lender. Available

title: U137 · Nothing changes without your approval

title: U144 · Read-only by design

title: U196 · Seats per plan
text: A seat is one named user's access to a product. Available

title: U197 · Unlimited-seat option
text: An unlimited-seat plan lets any number of people in an organisation use a product. Available

title: U187 · Serves brands across the UK, EU, US and Australia
text: Regional coverage describes the markets a product serves and the currencies it prices in. Available

title: U213 · Customer data kept separate

title: U214 · Your data is not used to train AI models
text: A no-training commitment states that the data you give a service is not used to train AI models. Available

title: U216 · Sub-processors disclosed
text: A sub-processor is a third party that processes customer data on a vendor's behalf. Disclosure means the vendor names them publicly. Available

title: U218 · Deletion and retention after you disconnect
text: Retention and deletion rules set out how long a vendor keeps your data and when it is removed after you stop using the service. Available

title: U219 · Read-only access scopes
text: An access scope is the set of permissions an app requests when you connect a platform. A read-only scope lets the app view data without changing it. Available · limited scope

title: M4 · Hosted on Google Cloud Platform
text: Hosting describes the cloud infrastructure a service runs on. Available

title: CO1 · Published pricing
text: Published pricing means plans and prices are shown publicly, so you can read them without talking to sales. Available

title: CO4 · Priced by seat
text: Seat-based pricing charges for the number of people who use a product. Available

title: CO5 · Price does not rise with your revenue
text: A pricing model in which growth in revenue or orders does not increase what you pay. Available

title: CO6 · Unlimited usage on every plan
text: Unlimited usage means a plan does not cap or meter how much you use the product. Available

title: CO15 · No integration fees
text: An integration fee is a charge for connecting a data source or building a custom connector. Available

title: CO17 · Compared with hiring an analyst
text: A way to judge a tool's cost against the cost of hiring a person to do similar work. Available

title: CO11 · Annual billing discount
text: An annual billing discount is a lower effective price for paying for a year at a time instead of monthly. Available

title: CO9 · Card and data connection at signup
text: Some products ask for payment details and a data connection when you create your account. Available

title: CO16 · Mastercard Business Bonus partner pricing
text: Partner pricing is a separate price list offered to members of a partner programme. For Luca, it is a dedicated pricing page for Mastercard Business Bonus merchants. Available

title: M5 · Organisation setup during signup
text: Organisation setup is the signup step where you create the account that represents your business before adding data. Available

title: S3 · Hands-on onboarding with Luca's team
text: Hands-on onboarding means the vendor's team does much of the setup work with you, rather than leaving you to configure the product alone. Available

title: S4 · Data mapping done by Luca's team
text: Data mapping is matching fields and records across systems so that figures from different sources line up. Available

title: S10 · Luca community
text: A customer community is a shared space where users and prospects exchange ideas about a product. Available

title: T18 · E-Commerce Leaders Series podcast
text: An owned podcast is a show a company produces itself. Luca's features conversations with e-commerce operators. Available

title: T14 · Founder background
text: Founder background describes the experience of the people leading a company. Available

title: R9 · Team
text: A named team shows who builds and runs a product. Available

title: R5 · AI model provider disclosed
text: Model provider disclosure means a vendor names the company whose language model its product uses. Available

title: R6 · Product velocity
text: Product velocity is how quickly a vendor ships and extends its product. Available

title: T8 · Customer logos
text: Customer logos show which brands a vendor names as customers. Available

title: T9 · Named testimonials
text: Named testimonials are customer statements published with the person's name and photograph. Available

title: FD1 · One place to see the whole business
text: A single view that brings a brand's data together so the business can be read in one place. In Luca, this view is called Numbers. Available

title: FD2 · Answers in plain English, no dashboards
text: Asking questions about business data in everyday language, instead of building reports or dashboards to find the answer. Available

title: FD10 · The analyst you cannot hire yet
text: Analytical help for a brand that needs analysis but is not yet ready to hire a full-time analyst or a fractional CFO. Available

title: FD11 · Never changes anything without my OK

title: FD17 · My data is not used to train AI

title: FD18 · Trial on my own data
text: Evaluating a product with your own business data from the start, rather than with sample data. Available

title: FD20 · What Luca sees beyond Shopify Sidekick
text: The difference between an assistant that works inside one platform and an analyst that reads data from several platforms together. Available

title: FD21 · Connected data instead of CSV exports
text: Analysing business data through live connections and stored context, rather than exporting files to a general chatbot each time. Available

title: FD29 · Talks to me like a co-founder
text: Working with business data through conversation, as you would with an analyst, rather than by reading a dashboard. Available

title: FD30 · A human to call when I'm stuck
text: Access to people who help you set up and use the product, not only self-serve software. Available

title: SU2 · Subscriptions, Shopify and accounting reconciled
text: Bringing subscription platform, store and accounting data into agreement so that one view of the business can be trusted. Available

title: SU3 · Active and lapsed subscribers

title: SU4 · Skips analysed (the $72,000 case)

title: CF18 · No money moves without approval

title: CF22 · Works with our accountant, keeps the ledger
text: An analysis tool that reads accounting data without replacing the accounting system as the record. Available

title: CF25 · Data retention after we leave
text: The terms that govern how long a provider keeps your data and when it is deleted after you stop using it. Available

title: CF1 · Revenue and margin reconcile to the accounts

title: CF2 · Accounting system connection

title: GR21 · Luca in Slack for the team
text: Using an analysis tool from inside Slack, so a team can ask questions where it already works. Available

title: GR23 · Google Analytics and Search Console alongside ads
text: Connecting web analytics and search data next to ad platform data, so traffic and spend can be read together. Available

title: MC1 · Shopify and Amazon in one P&L
text: Bringing sales from Shopify and Amazon into one profit and loss view of the business. Available · limited scope

title: EU4 · Prices in EUR and GBP

title: EU12 · Mastercard Business Bonus for European brands
text: A partner route to Luca for merchants in the Mastercard Business Bonus programme, relevant to European brands that take part. Available

title: EU3 · Xero and European banking sources
text: Connecting accounting systems and banking sources used by European brands, such as Xero, Exact and Open Banking. Available · limited scope

title: MB1 · Am I eligible?
text: Whether a merchant qualifies for Luca's Mastercard Business Bonus partner pricing. Available

title: MB2 · Size of the discount
text: How much the Mastercard Business Bonus partner discount reduces the price of Luca's plans. Available

title: MB4 · Listed on Mastercard Business Bonus
text: Being listed by a known partner programme, which gives merchants a recognisable place to find a provider. Available

title: MB6 · Same product as the full plan
text: Whether partner pricing buys the same product as standard pricing, or a reduced version. Available

title: SC8 · Unlimited seats
text: Unlimited seats means there is no cap on the number of users on a plan. Available
